items.followUp: Convert 25 °C into Fahrenheit using the Celsius–Fahrenheit relation.

rubric.why: Uses the correct relation between Celsius and Fahrenheit scales.
rubric.how: Award for the Celsius–Fahrenheit conversion formula.

rubric.why: Confirms the conversion and final temperature.
rubric.how: Award for the correct final temperature, 122 °F.

modelAnswer: Given: C = 50 °C.
Formula: F = 9/5 C + 32.
Substitution: F = 9/5(50) + 32 = 90 + 32.
Answer: F = 122 °F.

items.followUp: Using Newton's second law, derive the relation between force and the change in momentum of a body.

rubric.why: Starts the derivation with Newton's second law.
Expresses acceleration in terms of the change in velocity and time.
rubric.how: Award for the correct acceleration expression.

rubric.why: Substitutes the acceleration expression into Newton's second law.
rubric.how: Award for the correct substitution or its algebraic equivalent.

rubric.why: Uses the definition of momentum to reach the force–momentum relation.
rubric.description: Expresses force as the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award for identifying p = mv and stating the resulting relation.

modelAnswer: According to Newton's second law, F = ma.
For a body changing its velocity from u to v in time t, a = (v − u)/t.
Therefore, F = m(v − u)/t = (mv − mu)/t.
Since momentum p = mv, F = (p₂ − p₁)/t = Δp/t = change in momentum/time.

items.followUp: State Pascal's law and explain how a hydraulic lift multiplies force.

rubric.why: Includes the essential elements of Pascal's law.
rubric.how: Award for stating that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished.

rubric.why: Identifies the arrangement of the hydraulic press.
rubric.how: Award for identifying two pistons of different areas connected by liquid.

rubric.why: Applies Pascal's law to the two pistons.
rubric.how: Award for the equality of pressure at the pistons or its equivalent.

rubric.why: Explains how the press multiplies force.
rubric.how: Award for relating the larger piston area to a greater output force or load-lifting ability.

modelAnswer: Pascal's law: Pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions throughout the liquid and to the walls of its container.
A hydraulic press consists of two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.
By Pascal's law, the pressures at the pistons are equal: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂.
Since the larger piston has a greater area, it produces a greater force; thus, a small input force can lift a heavy load.

items.followUp: Define equilibrium and state the first condition for equilibrium for a body acted on by several forces.

rubric.why: Defines equilibrium in terms of balanced forces and their effect.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the forces are balanced or that the body has no acceleration.

rubric.why: States the possible motion of a body in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is at rest or moves with uniform velocity.

rubric.why: States the first condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the vector sum or resultant of all forces is zero.

rubric.why: Gives the component form of the zero-resultant condition in two dimensions.
rubric.how: Award for setting both perpendicular components of the resultant force to zero.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when its forces are balanced and it has no acceleration.
It is either at rest or moves with uniform velocity.
First condition for equilibrium: the resultant (vector sum) of all forces acting on the body must be zero, ΣF = 0.
In two dimensions, this requires ΣFₓ = 0 and ΣFᵧ = 0.

items.followUp: A pump lifts 150 kg of water through 8 m in 12 s. Calculate its power, taking g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: Identifies the data, including the gravitational acceleration used.
rubric.description: Lists the given quantities in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying the mass, height, time and g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: Uses power as work done per unit time and the work required to lift the water.
rubric.how: Award for a correct power formula for lifting the water.

rubric.why: Substitutes the values with appropriate units.
rubric.how: Award for correct substitution using the given quantities and g = 10 m/s².
Award for obtaining 1200 as the numerical value.

rubric.why: Requires the final power answer to include its unit.
rubric.how: Award for the final answer 1200 W.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 200 kg, h = 6 m, t = 10 s, g = 10 m/s².
Formula: P = W/t = mgh/t.
Substitution: P = (200 kg)(10 m/s²)(6 m)/(10 s).
P = 1200 kg·m²/s³.
Answer: P = 1200 W.
